- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above prior peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is falling, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment-driven reversal.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply 3–5 day lag correction: forecast = prior 3-day average + sentiment-weighted adjustment (0.3–0.7 multiplier).
- When sentiment is flat (0.0–0.2) and price is trending downward, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to counteract downward drift.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period when sentiment is neutral or negative; apply 1–2% downward correction for first 5–7 days.
